messages:
maya: :rotating_light: Observed multiple GPU containers crashing on node gpu-node-17 across the 18:00-18:10 window — OOMs reported even though allocator reports ~600MB spare buffer per GPU. Raising an incident.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20240315-97 (severity: high) — tagging #oncall-eng and paging current SRE.

liam: copying logs from the runtime:
```
[2024-03-15T18:02:12Z] [gpu0] alloc: request=1.2GiB free=640MiB reserved=512MiB
[2024-03-15T18:02:12Z] [gpu0] ERROR cudaMemcpy failed: out of memory
[2024-03-15T18:02:12Z] [serving] evict attempt -> failed (no contiguous block)
```

maya: interesting — reserved shows 512MiB but free shows 640MiB and yet allocation of 1.2GiB fails. Could be fragmentation / non-contiguous space.

tess: I'm oncall. I'm going to add customer impact: a handful of large-chat requests (~max tokens) started failing for some Dedicated customers. Metrics: error rate spiked to 6% for chat-gen on region-us-west-2 for ~8 minutes.

rachel: Which customers? Any SLA hits?

tess: preliminary list: cust-plat-17, fin-ops-qa, chat-app-beta. No formal SLA breach yet; we're still within 99th latency but error rate breach could escalate.

liam: quick triage steps I ran: disabled prefix KV caching on the failing shard (to rule out cache reservation mismatch) and restarted the runtime on gpu-node-17. After restart, node accepted requests for ~30s then started OOMing again.

maya: did you observe reserved pool reallocation after restart?

liam: reserve logs show: `reserve_shrink: triggered by host_reclaim(10%)` then `reserve_grow: blocking wait for evict`. Sequence suggests the reserve pool is oscillating due to concurrent small frees causing fragmentation.

maya: Can we trigger a compaction or force contiguous allocation path? Any kernel level support?

liam: runtime has a manual compaction command but it's disruptive: requires pausing new inflight batches. I proposed a rolling drain on the node to run compaction script.

tess: do it. Start with graceful drain on gpu-node-17. I'll coordinate customer-facing comms.

deploy-bot: @tess starting cordon/drain on gpu-node-17
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m

rachel: Suggest we also temporarily lower `max_sequence_length` for the heavy routes to reduce peak allocation. Can we patch the model config for the affected model id m-bert-7b?

liam: yes we can flip a route-level override; putting a quick patch now to cap max_tokens to 1024 for that model in us-west-2. Patch command:
```
api call: POST /v1/routes/override
body: {"route":"/v1/generate/m-bert-7b","max_tokens":1024}
```

maya: good mitigation. Also enable soft-fallback policy to route heavy requests to slower but lower-memory model variant (m-bert-7b-quant). That will reduce pressure.

liam: rolled the route override at 18:05:22. Fallback policy enabled at 18:06:01. Error rate dropped from 6% to ~1.1% over two minutes.

tess: customer comms draft: "We're investigating allocation failures affecting a small subset of large-generation requests in us-west-2. We've applied temporary mitigations including routing to a lower-memory model and draining one node. We'll update within 30 minutes." Approve? :eyes:

rachel: approve, send.

incident-bot: @oncall — postmortem template created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20240315-97

liam: post-drain inspection on gpu-node-17: free memory map shows many small free segments <64MiB and a handful of large segments ~200-300MiB separated by pinned allocations (KV cache shards). Looks like fragmentation from repeated reserve_shrink/grow events.

maya: are pinned allocations coming from ephemeral background jobs or steady-state KV cache?

liam: both. We found a daemon on the node doing background embedding prefetch that holds pinned buffers until checkpoint; it was recently updated to keep a larger prefetch window. Marking that as suspect.

maya: action items: 1) revert prefetch window to previous value on background daemon (rachel) 2) tune reserve policy to avoid aggressive shrink/grow hysteresis (liam) 3) schedule compaction on drained node (maya) 4) run a short capacity test to verify stability (tess).

rachel: reverting prefetch setting now (rolling restart of embedding-daemon via systemd). Command: `systemctl restart embedding-prefetcher` — doing a 2-minute stagger.

liam: I'll file a runtime config patch to add a 30s cooldown on reserve adjustments and increase minimum contiguous reservation to 1GiB to avoid tiny blocks causing allocation failure. Patch PR created: https://git.internal/runtime/pulls/4221

maya: compaction scheduled at 18:20 UTC on gpu-node-17 once drained. We'll run `runtime-compact --force --threshold=64MiB` and monitor. Expect a brief pause in new allocations.

deploy-bot: drain completed; pods evicted. Node cordoned.

liam: compaction run started at 18:21:12. Output snippet:
```
compact: scanned 1.2GiB free fragments, merged -> 1.05GiB contiguous freed
compact: relocated 3 pinned buffers temporarily to staging, success
compact: finished in 18s
```

maya: good. Starting node bring-up at 18:21:45.

rachel: embedding-prefetcher restart finished on gpu-node-17 at 18:22:30. Prefetch window now 2x smaller.

tess: monitoring customer errors and latency: at 18:25 error rate back to baseline 0.2%. No ongoing SLA impacts currently. I'll keep the incident open for tracking follow-ups.

maya: root cause hypothesis: combination of increased background prefetch leading to pinned shards plus aggressive reserve pool shrink/grow causing fragmentation that prevented large contiguous allocations. OOMs happened when large-generation requests needed a contiguous allocation bigger than any free run even though total free memory looked sufficient.

liam: mitigation summary posted to runbook: immediately reduce prefetch, enable fallback routes for heavy requests, apply reserve cooldown, run compaction on fragmented nodes. I'll add the compaction flag to the autoscaler for nodes that hit repeated reserve oscillation.

rachel: follow-ups: 1) telemetry: add contiguous-free-run metric to GPU exporter, 2) add an alert when reserve_shrink/grow toggles >3x in 5m, 3) schedule a targeted test to reproduce fragmentation pattern with synthetic traffic.

incident-bot: Incident update: severity downgraded to medium at 18:28 UTC.

maya: thanks everyone. Keeping this thread open for the post-incident review. I'll convert the incident ticket to a follow-up with owners for the three action items. :thumbsup:
